newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bond prices close up on lower inflation.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bond prices close up on lower inflation.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed higher on Wednesday, with the exception of inflation-linked short bonds, as the market celebrated news of lower inflation and expectations of an interest rate cut, traders said.
* CPI (consumer price index) linked government bonds: +0.1 pct to 168.00
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.2 pct to 166.72
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 pct at 158.21

"In general, there was bid demand for inflation-indexed bonds and the market generally rose," said Roy Meir of Simodan Investments. Medium- and long-term CPI bonds benefitted from the latest inflation news as did unlinked bonds.

The only segment to run against the trend was CPI-linked short bonds, said Danni Scharia of Capital Holdings. Dollar-linked bond benefitted from a stronger U.S. currency in local forex trading, he said, with the index rising 0.4 percent. The dollar gained 0.2 percent to close at 3.2030 shekels, although it was off its high for the day.
The prospects of a reduction in interest rates have grown after Tuesday's release of the September CPI, which rose only 0.4 percent.

In addition, Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel said he would take into account the slowing of the economy in determining monetary policy, a stand that could be influenced by the release on Wednesday of new Central Bureau of Statistics estimates. The bureau said gross domestic product would grow only 3.8 percent this year.
Scharia said the market was now expecting the central bank to cut the base short-term rate by up to 0.5 percentage point on October 28. The rate is currently 15.5 percent.
At 171 million shekels (including trading in the Makam), turnover in the bond market was average compared to recent days, Meir said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity. ($1= 3.20 shekels)
